title: Apple is shuttering its 28-year-old online community forum
gist: Apple is permanently closing its 28-year-old Apple Support Community forum on November 20, 2026, after reviewing its support strategy, steering users toward official Apple support. The forum may also have lost relevance to rivals like Reddit, MacRumors and AppleInsider.

insights.claim: Apple will permanently close its Apple Support Community forum on November 20, 2026; it became read-only immediately upon the announcement.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Minor operational change; signals Apple centralizing customer support channels.
insights.locator: Apple’s online community forum will close

insights.claim: Apple reportedly told MacRumors it is shutting the forum after evaluating its support strategy and customer needs, suggesting it now prefers customers rely on official Apple staff for support.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Apple is pulling support toward controlled official channels.

insights.claim: The Apple Support Community began in 1998 as Apple Tech Exchange, became Apple Discussions in 2000 and Apple Support Communities in 2011 before its current name.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.locator: The Apple Support Community dates to 1998

insights.claim: The forum may have become less popular as third-party communities such as Reddit and the MacRumors and AppleInsider forums grew.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: User-generated tech support continues to migrate to third-party platforms like Reddit.
